clue.text: Snobby Channel Islander upset losing learned supply

indicators.note: upset says the letters of Channel Islander are thrown into disorder
losing says the letters of learned must be taken out of the mixed pool
supply, read as 'supplely' or flexibly, says the letters of learned are taken in any order

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder for the composite anagram
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A stuck-up islander from Jersey or Guernsey sulks about losing a supply of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a composite anagram: the letters of CHANNEL ISLANDER are exactly those of the answer plus those of LEARNED, so rearranging what is left after removing LEARNED gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clannish group keeps to itself and looks down on outsiders, which is a snobbish attitude.

clue.text: Indelicate at heart, American made Oscar angry

indicators.note: at heart points to the central letter of the word for indelicate, the one being changed
made says that central letter is turned into a different one

parts.note: crass means grossly insensitive or indelicate
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tactless American turned the Oscars ceremony into a furious row.
explanation.walkthrough: Take CRASS (indelicate) and replace its middle letter A (American) with O (Oscar).
explanation.definitionFit: Cross is an everyday British synonym for annoyed or bad-tempered.

clue.text: George's car scheme takes one in

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car

indicators.note: takes ... in says one piece is drawn inside another, here the numeral goes into the scheme
completes the containment phrase takes ... in

parts.note: a plot is a scheme
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: George's plan for his car involves taking a passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: George is RAF and aviation slang for an aircraft's autopilot; the 's is the link 'has' in the surface reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots nicknamed the automatic flight-control system George, so the slang name stands for the device.

clue.text: Report led to the North getting share

indicators.note: getting joins the two parts, the first acquiring the second after it
in a down clue, going to the north means reading upwards, so the word for led is written backwards

parts.note: ran, as in ran a business, means led
a ration is a person's allotted share

explanation.surface: A report says someone led the northern region to win its share of resources.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the answer reads top to bottom, so 'to the North' means writing upwards, a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A narration is a spoken or written account, a report of events.

clue.text: Opening of some Pinots is rather a labour — send for corkscrews

indicators.note: opening of each word means its first letter, taken in turn across the seven words

explanation.surface: Uncorking some Pinot Noir is such hard work that you send out for a corkscrew.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of Some Pinots Is Rather A Labour Send spell the answer; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to corkscrew is to twist round in a helix, which is what something does when it spirals.

clue.text: Superweapon chosen involves cloak

indicators.note: involves says the phrase Superweapon chosen contains the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A superweapon has been chosen, and it comes with a cloak, as in a spy thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: A poncho is a sleeveless outer garment draped over the shoulders, a kind of cloak.

clue.text: Returning alumnae consume bottles — a vast quantity

indicators.note: Returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
bottles, as a verb, says the phrase alumnae consume holds the letters inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Former students coming back for a reunion drink bottles in vast quantities.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'bottles' into the definition, but it is the verb that signals the hidden letters (the phrase bottles them); the definition is only 'a vast quantity', as in oceans of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean of something, or oceans of it, is an informal way of saying a huge amount.

clue.text: Cunning cricketer cleared out tail-end

indicators.note: cleared out means the inside of cricketer is emptied, leaving just its first and last letters

parts.note: aft is the rear or tail end, as of a ship

explanation.surface: A wily cricketer has knocked over the tail-end batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the tail-end is the weak last batsmen, which makes 'tail-end' look like part of the cricket scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft as a noun means skill in deceiving, guile or cunning.

clue.text: Defeated and dismissed, allowed to run out around lake

parts.note: a batsman who is dismissed is out

indicators.note: around says the phrase for allowed to run out goes round the letter for lake

parts.note: a rope is payed out when it is let run out
L is a common map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A batsman was beaten and dismissed, run out somewhere near a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: PAYED (the nautical spelling used for paying out rope) wraps round L.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outplayed is to be beaten by a stronger opponent in a game.

clue.text: Quiet British drive the French in retreat

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the words for drive and the French are read in reverse

parts.note: to drive a golf ball is to hit it, and put can mean to drive or thrust
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A quiet British driver heads for France, then backs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quiet' is a command here, the definition: belt up is British slang for shut up.
explanation.definitionFit: Belt up is a British slang command to shut up, an order for quiet.

clue.text: Fur too much, Vera discovered

parts.note: OTT stands for over the top, meaning excessive

indicators.note: discovered means the covering outer letters of Vera are stripped away

explanation.surface: Vera has revealed too much fur, a fashion faux pas.
explanation.definitionFit: Otter is the pelt of the aquatic mammal, sold as a fur.

clue.text: Being a member of English stage, Dec's partner is crude

parts.note: to be in a club is to be a member of it
a leg is a stage of a journey or race
Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting duo, so Dec's partner is Ant

explanation.surface: Ant, Dec's partner on the English stage, is said to be crude.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a long-running British television double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking grace or refinement, so it can describe something crude.

clue.text: After excellent exercise, son turns brown

indicators.note: turns says the run of letters for excellent, exercise and son is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as the letter I
PE is physical education, exercise at school
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: After a great workout, a son goes brown with a tan.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 written as AI is a common crossword device for excellent. AIPES read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown pigment, the tint of old photographs, so it names a shade of brown.

clue.text: A Nationalist, a Liberal holding PM's Downing St address before Labour, perhaps

indicators.note: holding says the word for Nationalist contains the PM's address

parts.note: the Prime Minister lives at Number 10 Downing Street

explanation.surface: Political parties line up at Number 10 ahead of the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital L makes Labour look like the party; the definition means before childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenatal means relating to pregnancy before birth, the period before labour, the process of childbirth.

clue.text: Capital vans of Victor's independent lot never include used specimens

indicators.note: the van is the front, so the vans of these words are their first letters

parts.words: Victor's independent lot never include used specimens

explanation.surface: Victor's car dealership never puts second-hand vans on show.
explanation.definitionFit: Vilnius is the capital city of Lithuania.

clue.text: Parts of supporting column peak mostly by Scottish hillside

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word for peak is used

parts.note: a vertex is the highest point or peak
brae is a Scots word for a hillside

explanation.surface: Bits of a supporting pillar are found near a peak on a Scottish hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertebrae are the bones that make up the spinal column, the body's supporting column.

clue.text: Fine plan, yet messed up

indicators.note: messed up says the letters of plan and yet are jumbled

explanation.surface: A good plan, yet it went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Fine looks like an adjective praising the plan, but it is the noun for a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine is a sum paid as punishment, which is a penalty.

clue.text: Perhaps amateur match for charity

parts.note: an amateur is an example of a non-pro, someone not professional
to fit is to match or suit

explanation.surface: An amateur match is being played to raise money for charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests a game but here means fit, as in suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonprofit organisation exists for public benefit rather than gain, like a charitable body.

clue.text: Take care of appearance later

parts.note: a look is an appearance
after means later

explanation.surface: Look after your appearance in later life.
explanation.definitionFit: To look after someone is to tend to them, a common phrasal verb for caring.

clue.text: Train bird to accept one sent back

indicators.note: to accept says the bird takes the reversed word inside it

parts.note: a ree is a female ruff, a wading bird (also called a reeve)

indicators.note: sent back means the word for one is written in reverse

parts.note: a unit is a single thing, one

explanation.surface: Teaching a bird to take back something returned.
explanation.walkthrough: REE, a rare name for the female ruff, holds TINU, which is UNIT reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the train of attendants following an important person.

clue.text: Run out of more books for living

indicators.note: out of says the letter for run is removed from the combined word

parts.note: extra means more
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: We have run out of further books to live on.
explanation.walkthrough: EXTRA plus NT gives EXTRANT; take out R.
explanation.definitionFit: Extant means still in existence, surviving, so still living.

clue.text: Perhaps mouldy lid uncovered after entertaining bash

indicators.note: after says the trimmed lid follows the words for entertaining and bash

parts.note: fun means entertaining
to have a bash is to have a go

indicators.note: uncovered means the first letter, the top cover, of lid is removed

explanation.surface: A mouldy lid is uncovered after a fun party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bash' suggests a party but here means an attempt, a GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Fungoid means like a fungus, and mould is a type of fungus, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Spare appropriate to Paddington, maybe

parts.note: for can mean suitable or appropriate to, as in fit for purpose
Paddington is the famous fictional bear from Peru, an example of a bear

explanation.surface: A spare item suitable for Paddington, perhaps a marmalade sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: Spare is a verb here: forbear means to refrain from, as in spare me the details.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to refrain or hold back from something, like to spare someone a punishment.

clue.text: Key area at some time spoken of as way to get a rise?

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

indicators.note: spoken of says the word for at some time is what is heard when the letters are said

parts.note: later means at some future time

explanation.surface: The key area at some point is described as a route to a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, ESC A LATER runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalator is a moving staircase that carries people upwards, a literal rise.

clue.text: Modest, no time for pursuit

indicators.note: no time means without the letter for time, so it is removed

parts.note: chaste means pure or modest

explanation.surface: Modest, with no time for pursuits.
explanation.definitionFit: A chase is the act of hunting down or pursuing someone.

clue.text: Ghastly top worn by primitive beginner?

indicators.note: worn by here says the top is wrapped around the primitive prefix

parts.note: a lid is a top
ur- is a prefix, a word beginning, meaning original or primitive

explanation.surface: A beginner in primitive times wore a ghastly top.
explanation.walkthrough: The ? flags that the beginner is the beginning of a word: the prefix UR as in Ursprache.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid means shockingly vivid or horrifying, like ghastly details.

clue.text: Official beginning to mow field

parts.note: real can mean genuine or official, as in the real thing

indicators.note: beginning to mow means its first letter only

explanation.surface: An official starts mowing a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a sphere or domain of activity, a field of study or work.

clue.text: Male King's schoolteacher provides delicious food

parts.note: Anna is the schoolteacher to the King of Siam in The King and I

explanation.surface: A man who teaches at King's School provides tasty meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna is the food from heaven in Exodus, figuratively any delightful sustenance.

clue.text: Republican bishop welcomed by curious Aegean order once more

indicators.note: welcomed by says the bishop's letters are taken inside the jumbled Aegean
curious, meaning odd, says the letters of Aegean are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A Republican bishop is warmly received in the Aegean, a curious arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange is to put things in order again, a different arrangement.

clue.text: Place to sleep following university, not coming back

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: coming back says the word not is read backwards

explanation.surface: After university, someone won't be returning to a place to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese-style mattress used as a bed.

clue.text: Corrects editor covering soldiers with sarcasm at first

indicators.note: covering says the editor's letters enclose the word for soldiers

parts.note: men are ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of sarcasm

explanation.surface: An editor tackles soldiers with sarcasm, at least initially.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to make corrections to a text, as an editor does.

clue.text: Racier, it breaks rules

indicators.note: breaks says the letters of Racier and it are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Racier behaviour breaks the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are standards or principles for judging, essentially rules.
